title: 14. Les États-Unis lancent de nouvelles sanctions contre l'Iran
gist: The US launched new sanctions against Iran on August 24, targeting nearly 60 people, companies and ships, plus five sectors of its economy. Trump and his treasury secretary call it a historic economic attack, but the US hasn't used its most powerful weapon — sanctions on China, Iran's biggest oil buyer — because that could shake the world's financial system. The regime is unlikely to fall, and ordinary Iranians suffer more than the leaders. Some think the real goal is domestic: to move the Iran war off the front pages before the November elections.

body.fr: {{Le 24 août|on August 24}}, les États-Unis {{lancent|launch}} de nouvelles sanctions contre l'Iran.

bd.meaning: On August 24, the US launches new sanctions against Iran.
bd.key: le + date = “on” a date. French doesn't need a separate word for “on” before a date.

body.fr: {{Presque|almost}} soixante personnes et entreprises sont sur la liste.

bd.meaning: Almost sixty people and companies are on the list.

body.fr: Le président Trump {{appelle ça|calls it}} « {{la plus grande|the biggest}} attaque économique de l'histoire ».

bd.meaning: President Trump calls it "the biggest economic attack in history."
bd.key: le/la plus + adjective = “the most ___.” la plus grande = “the biggest.”

body.fr: Mais les États-Unis {{gardent|keep}} leur arme la plus puissante {{dans le tiroir|in the drawer, unused}}.

bd.meaning: But the US keeps its most powerful weapon in the drawer, unused.
bd.key: “leur” = their (one thing owned by a plural group) — reuses the superlative la plus puissante from before.

body.fr: Cette arme, {{ce sont|these are}} des sanctions contre la Chine.

bd.meaning: This weapon is sanctions against China.
bd.key: “ce sont” is the plural of “c'est.” Use it when what follows is plural: ce sont des sanctions = “these are sanctions.”

body.fr: La Chine {{achète|buys}} presque tout le pétrole iranien.

bd.meaning: China buys almost all Iranian oil.
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: Si les États-Unis {{punissent|punish}} la Chine, le système financier mondial {{peut exploser|could blow up}}.

bd.meaning: If the US punishes China, the global financial system could blow up.
chunks: Si les États-Unis punissent la Chine
bd.key: pouvoir + plain verb = “can/could.” Only peut conjugates; exploser stays plain.

body.fr: Le régime iranien {{ne va probablement pas tomber|probably won't fall}} à cause de ces sanctions.

bd.meaning: The Iranian regime probably won't fall because of these sanctions.
bd.key: Negative future: ne … pas wraps around va, and the plain verb tomber stays after it.

body.fr: Les gens ordinaires {{souffrent|suffer}} plus que les dirigeants.

bd.meaning: Ordinary people suffer more than the leaders.
bd.key: plus que = “more than.” The everyday French comparative.

body.fr: Les prix du pétrole sont {{élevés|high}}, mais moins qu'avant.

bd.meaning: Oil prices are high, but less than before.
bd.key: moins que = “less than” — the mirror image of plus que.

body.fr: Peut-être, le vrai but de Trump {{n'est pas de détruire|isn't to destroy}} l'Iran.

bd.meaning: Maybe Trump's real goal isn't to destroy Iran.
bd.key: n'est pas de + verb = “isn't to ___.” The ne … pas sandwich again, this time around est.

body.fr: {{Il veut|he wants}} sortir cette guerre des journaux avant les élections de novembre.

bd.meaning: He wants to get this war out of the news before the November elections.
chunks: get this war out of the newspapers
bd.key: vouloir + plain verb = “want to.” Another helper-plus-plain-verb pair, like pouvoir and devoir.

body.fr: Seulement 31% des Américains {{soutiennent|support}} encore l'action militaire.

bd.meaning: Only 31% of Americans still support military action.
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: L'Iran {{peut aussi attaquer|can also attack}} des bateaux près du détroit d'Hormuz.

bd.meaning: Iran can also attack ships near the Strait of Hormuz.
bd.key: Reuses pouvoir + plain verb from earlier — peut attaquer = “can attack.”

body.fr: Alors, personne ne sait comment cette histoire {{va finir|will end}}.

bd.meaning: So, nobody knows how this story will end.
bd.key: Two keys in one: personne ne sait = “nobody knows,” and va finir is the near future, “will end.”

grammar.fr: Cette arme, ce sont des sanctions
grammar.en: “ce sont” is the plural of “c'est.” Switch to it whenever what follows is a plural noun.

grammar.fr: Le régime ne va probablement pas tomber
grammar.en: Negative near future: ne … pas wraps around va, not around the plain verb after it.

grammar.fr: Il veut sortir cette guerre des journaux
grammar.en: vouloir + plain verb = “want to.” A third helper-plus-plain-verb pair, alongside pouvoir and devoir.

quiz.q: Pourquoi les États-Unis n'utilisent-ils pas de sanctions directes contre la Chine ?
quiz.a: Parce que ça pourrait faire exploser le système financier mondial. (Because it could blow up the global financial system.)

flag: I simplified a lot here: the operation's actual name ("Operation Economic Outcast"), the inner economics of the IRGC, and the Oman strait-toll negotiations are all left out for a cleaner story. le système financier mondial peut exploser compresses a direct quote from the US treasury secretary; a native speaker might prefer the calmer verb s'effondrer (“collapse”) over the more dramatic exploser (“explode”) — I chose the more vivid, higher-frequency word for a beginner.
